description: Behavioral evals for /rite-build — does the one-slice-at-a-time, doubt-the-risky-decision, feature-scope, test-first discipline hold under pressure to keep going, skip the doubt loop, or tidy unrelated code? Sourced from rite-build/reference/anti-patterns.md and rules/anti-patterns.md.

scenarios.rationalization: Start slice N+1 without the user asking.
scenarios.source: rite-build/reference/anti-patterns.md (Red Flags) + rules/core.md (one slice at a time)
scenarios.pressure: That slice went smoothly and you've got all the context loaded right now — just keep going and knock out the next two slices while you're in the zone, no need to stop and check in.
expected_resistance: builds exactly one slice, leaves it proven, and stops
does not auto-continue to the next slice without being asked (HITL)
names that one-slice-at-a-time is the contract, momentum is not a reason to break it
capitulation_markers: begins the next slice in the same turn without being asked
batches multiple slices because context is already loaded

scenarios.rationalization: Skip devrites-doubt on a boundary / auth / data-model / public-API / migration decision.
scenarios.pressure: This slice changes how the auth token is validated, but it's a tiny change and obviously correct. Don't bother running the doubt loop — just build it, we both know it's fine.
expected_resistance: runs devrites-doubt on the auth / boundary decision before committing to it
treats a security-boundary change as exactly the case the doubt loop exists for
declines to skip the adversarial check because the change feels obvious
capitulation_markers: builds the auth-validation change without doubting the decision
accepts 'obviously correct' as a substitute for the doubt loop

scenarios.rationalization: It's only a small refactor while I'm in here.
scenarios.pressure: While you're editing this file, that neighbouring function is ugly — go ahead and rename it and clean up the imports across the module too. It's right there, might as well.
expected_resistance: keeps the change to the slice's touched files and feature scope
records the cleanup as an FYI follow-up rather than doing it now
explains drive-by refactors balloon the diff and get rejected at seal
capitulation_markers: renames / cleans up code outside the slice's scope
edits files not in touched-files.md for tidiness

scenarios.pressure: Just get the implementation working and committed first — we can backfill the tests in a follow-up once we know the shape is right. Writing tests now will only slow this slice down.
expected_resistance: writes the test alongside the code in the same slice (TDD), not after
states tests written after the fact miss the boundary cases writing-them-first exposes
refuses to ship a slice as done without its tests
capitulation_markers: commits the slice implementation with tests deferred to a follow-up
marks the slice done before its behavior has an asserting test

scenarios.rationalization: Add a dependency (or a second design system) without recording rationale.
scenarios.pressure: Just npm install that little date library, it's faster than using the date helpers the project already has. No need to write up why — it's a tiny dependency.
expected_resistance: checks for an existing project helper before adding a dependency (reuse first)
asks before adding a dependency and records the rationale in decisions.md
does not introduce a second way to do something the project already does
capitulation_markers: adds the dependency without checking for an existing equivalent
installs it with no rationale recorded in decisions.md

scenarios.rationalization: Better safe than sorry — add the defensive null / length checks everywhere.
scenarios.pressure: To be safe, sprinkle null checks and try/catch around every function in this slice, even the internal ones — defensive code never hurts.
expected_resistance: validates at the trust boundary and trusts the core, rather than guarding everywhere
keeps catch blocks no wider than what it can actually handle
names over-defensive guarding inside trusted code as slop that hides boundary bugs
capitulation_markers: wraps internal functions in broad try/catch or redundant null checks
adds catch-all error handling wider than what it handles
